title: Halting behavior of a return instruction
statement: Let $m$ be the number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a set of program states, and let $A$ assign an instruction to each state. Fix an initial state $l_*$, an oracle on Boolean words, an input word $x$, register values $v\colon\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\mathbb{N}$, an output word, and an integer $W\ge 0$. If the instruction at $l$ returns the Boolean value $b$, then the compiled program, started in state $l$ with those register values and output, reaches a halting configuration whose output is the given output word followed by $b$, with every register head position between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive. At every earlier step no call state is visited and all register head positions lie in that same interval.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction assignment $A$ and initial state $l_*$
The oracle on words and its index set
The state $l$ and Boolean return value $b$
